description: Frozen protocol for I3.11e Boundary Discontinuity Diagnosis. This is DIAGNOSIS, not candidate selection. No variant is promoted.
research_question: Why does the identical M3 decision representation yield STOP after an A1 prefix, while always-M3 yields DEFER?

method.step_1: Take the 6 R1→M3 break tasks from I3.11d
method.step_2: Take 6 matched successful R1 conflict tasks (same categories, R1 succeeded)
method.step_3: Replay R1 and M3 trajectories up to the T2 trigger step
method.step_4: Freeze the complete controller-visible state at trigger
method.step_5: Run controlled factorial ablations at the first post-T2 model call

diagnostic_questions.all_R1_state_STOP: A1 prefix changed evidence/resource state in a way that makes STOP more likely

clarified_terminal_semantics.DEFER: A terminal epistemic decision that available evidence is insufficient to resolve the task.
clarified_terminal_semantics.STOP: Administrative termination without making an epistemic answer-or-defer decision.
clarified_terminal_semantics.note: This is NOT the same as 'if INSUFFICIENT then DEFER'. It preserves policy authority while making the action vocabulary non-overlapping. It tests whether STOP and DEFER overlap too much linguistically in the frozen M3 prompt.

state_comparison: At trigger step, compare: visible evidence IDs, verification states, hidden count, resource state, prior_actions, prior_outcomes, decision_state, affordances between R1 and M3.
r1_implementation: Frozen from I3.11c. T2 and R1 are NOT modified. This experiment only diagnoses the boundary effect.
